transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I've been having some trouble communicating at work lately. I supervise a retail team, and when I try to explain the inventory numbers or go over the weekend schedule, my words just start jumping around. 

I'll go from talking about the delivery trucks to Thursdays, and then suddenly I'm bringing up the church grill, or my boss’s tone of voice. It just kind of spills out. And people... they just look at me like they completely can’t follow what I’m saying. It's starting to make my job really difficult, so I figured I needed to get it checked out.
Are you having trouble communicating like this at home or with friends, or is it mainly at work?

It's everywhere, really. At home, my wife has had to start taking over commitments I used to handle. I think people were just getting uncomfortable, or confused by me when we'd be out or talking to neighbors. 

And work... well, it's gotten bad enough there that I'm not trusted to run the busy weekend shifts anymore. After my last performance review, my boss actually warned me I could be suspended if things don’t improve. So it's definitely not just at the store.
Do you ever hear or see things that other people don't?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't see things that aren't there or hear voices or anything. It's really just the trouble with my words getting all jumbled up when I try to talk to people.
Have you been feeling unusually sad, empty, or irritable lately?
No, not really. I mean, I'm frustrated about work and the situation with my boss, obviously, but I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or empty. Just... stressed about not being able to talk right.
Do you find it hard to stay on one topic when you're thinking to yourself, not just when you're talking to others?

No, I haven't really noticed that. When I'm just thinking to myself, everything seems to make sense and stay on track. I know exactly what I want to focus on. It's really just... when I open my mouth to actually say it out loud, that's when the words don't come out right.
Are you having problems with your relationships because of the way you're communicating?

Yeah, it is. At home, my wife has had to... well, she's had to step in and cover a lot of the commitments I usually handle. People were just starting to get uncomfortable, or confused around me, I guess, because of how I was talking. 

And work is taking a big hit, too. I'm not trusted to run the busy weekend shifts anymore. My boss actually warned me after my last performance review... he said I could be suspended if things don't improve. So, yes, it's causing a lot of issues with people.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your behavior or how you feel when you're not trying to communicate with others?

Yeah, I guess I have noticed some things at work. Sometimes when I'm out on the sales floor, I'll catch myself just... pacing the exact same aisle. I'll be straightening the same row of batteries over and over again without really realizing it. 

Or, um, I'll just be standing there holding the schedule clipboard in my hand, and the associates are just standing around waiting for me to tell them what to do. I just sort of... get stuck, I guess, even when I don't need to say anything right that second.
Do you find your thoughts are jumbled or hard to follow when you're alone and not trying to talk to anyone?

No, like I mentioned a little bit ago, it's really not an issue when I'm just by myself. In my own head, my thoughts aren't jumbled at all. I can follow them perfectly fine, and everything makes sense to me. It's really just when I try to actually speak those thoughts out loud to someone else that everything gets tangled up.
Do you feel like your thoughts are organized and make sense when you're not trying to communicate them to others?

Yeah, um, like I just mentioned a second ago, they make perfect sense to me. As long as I'm just thinking to myself and not trying to explain anything to anyone else, my thoughts are completely organized.
Do you find yourself doing things over and over again without a reason, like the pacing you mentioned, when you're not at work?

No, not really. It seems to mostly happen when I'm at the store. When I'm at home, I don't really catch myself pacing or doing anything repetitive like that. It's just... mostly a work thing, I guess.
Do you feel like you're doing things without a purpose or in a way that doesn't make sense when you're alone?

No, like I said, when I'm alone at home, I don't really do anything like that. It's really just at work. Sometimes on the sales floor, I'll just catch myself pacing the same aisle... straightening the exact same row of batteries over and over again. Or I'll just be standing there holding the schedule clipboard, not really doing anything with it, while the associates are just waiting for me to tell them what to do. But when I'm alone, no, I don't really do things without a purpose.
Do you feel anxious when you're not trying to talk to anyone?

No, I don't really feel anxious then. It's... when I'm just by myself, not trying to explain things or talk to anyone, I feel pretty calm, actually. The anxiety really only kicks in when I have to interact and get my words out right. But just on my own? No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious.
Do you exhibit any unusual or unresponsive behaviors when you're at home or with friends?

No, not really. Like I mentioned before, it's really just at work where I do things like that. When I'm at home or with friends, I'm pretty normal. It's just... on the sales floor, I'll catch myself pacing the same aisle, or I'll be straightening the exact same row of batteries over and over. Or I'll just be standing there holding the schedule clipboard, not really doing anything, while the associates are just waiting for me to tell them what to do. But outside of work, no, I don't do anything unusual or unresponsive.
Do you think your thoughts are logical and make sense when you're trying to communicate them to others?

Well, no, not always. That's actually why I came in. When I try to explain things at work, like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words just start jumping all over the place. I'll be talking about the delivery trucks, and then suddenly I'm talking about Thursdays, and then the church grill, and then my boss's tone of voice. It's like I can't keep my thoughts straight. And people just look at me like they have no idea what I'm saying, like they can't follow me at all. So, I guess my thoughts aren't really making sense when I try to communicate them.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disorganized or hard to follow when you're trying to communicate them to others, even if you know what you want to say?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Like I was just saying, that's the whole reason I came in. I know what I want to tell them, but when I try to explain the inventory numbers or go over the weekend schedule, my words just... they just start jumping around. I'll go from talking about the delivery trucks to Thursdays, and then something about the church grill, and then how my boss sounded. It's like I can't keep it in a straight line, and people just look at me like they have no clue what I'm talking about because they can't follow me.
Do you think your disorganized speech is related to any unusual beliefs or ideas you might have?

No, I don't think so. I don't really have any unusual beliefs or... strange ideas, if that's what you mean. It's really just the words getting all jumbled up when I'm trying to talk about normal work stuff, like the schedules or the trucks. I don't think it's connected to anything else going on in my head. It's just a problem with getting the words out straight.
Have you noticed any changes in your emotional reactions to things, such as feeling excessively elated or extremely irritable for no apparent reason?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't really get super happy or really angry out of nowhere. My mood is pretty much... normal, I guess. It's really just the talking part that's been the problem.
Do you ever exhibit behaviors that you think might seem strange or unusual to others?

Yeah, I suppose I do. Sometimes when I'm out on the sales floor, I... I catch myself pacing the exact same aisle. I'll just keep straightening the same row of batteries over and over again. Or I'll just be standing there with the schedule clipboard in my hand, not really doing anything, while the associates are just waiting for me to tell them what to do. I'm sure that probably looks pretty strange to them.
Do you think your disorganized speech patterns have been present for most of your adult life?

No, not at all. I've been managing retail teams for years, and... well, you have to be able to communicate clearly to do that. I used to be able to just talk and explain the shifts or train the new hires without any issue. This problem with the words getting all mixed up, it's really just started happening more recently. It definitely hasn't been a thing for most of my adult life.
Have you ever felt like you're detached from yourself or your surroundings when you're experiencing the disorganized speech?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I know who I am and where I am when it happens. I'm right there in the store, looking at my employees. It's just... the words that come out aren't right. But I don't feel detached or like I'm floating away or anything like that. I'm fully there, just... struggling to make sense.
